questions.questionText: What are the two primary physical components used to build the kinematic chain of a robotic arm?

options.text: Pistons and gears
Links and joints
Sensors and end-effectors
Actuators and drivers

questions.questionText: Which type of joint permits translational sliding motion along a single linear axis?

options.text: Revolute joint
Spherical joint
Prismatic joint
Universal joint

questions.questionText: What does "Degrees of Freedom" (DOF) represent in robotic manipulation?

options.text: The maximum weight a robot can carry
The total number of motors installed on the robot
The number of independent parameters required to define its configuration
The speed at which the robot arm can move through space

questions.questionText: What defines the "workspace" of a robotic arm?

options.text: The physical dimensions of the laboratory floor
The geometric volume that the robot's end-effector can reach
The maximum electrical power output of the joint motors
The surface area of the gripper jaws

questions.questionText: Which factor directly limits the maximum reachable workspace of a robotic arm?

options.text: Joint limits and physical link lengths
The thickness of the power supply cables
The processing speed of the microcontroller
The programming language used to code the robot

questions.questionText: In 3D Cartesian space, how many parameters are required to fully define both the position and orientation of a rigid body?

options.text: 3 (3 translation)
4 (2 translation, 2 rotation)
6 (3 translation, 3 rotation)
9 (3 translation, 6 rotation)

questions.questionText: What is calculated during Forward Kinematics?

options.text: The joint torque required to balance a target load
The joint angles needed to reach a desired target coordinate
The Cartesian position and orientation of the tool given known joint angles
The electrical current drawn by the motor driver

questions.questionText: What is calculated during Inverse Kinematics (IK)?

options.text: The Cartesian end-effector position from given joint angles
The required joint angles to place the end-effector at a desired Cartesian target
The frictional forces between the gripper and the object
The maximum payload velocity during movement

questions.questionText: Why might an Inverse Kinematics solver return multiple valid solutions for a single Cartesian pose?

options.text: Because the robot is disconnected from power
Because multiple joint configurations (e.g., elbow-up vs. elbow-down) can reach the same coordinate
Because Cartesian space is two-dimensional
Because revolute joints cannot rotate continuously

questions.questionText: What occurs when an Inverse Kinematics target is located outside the arm's workspace?

options.text: The robot executes the movement at twice its normal speed
The IK algorithm produces no valid real mathematical solution
The end-effector automatically expands to reach the target
The revolute joints temporarily transform into prismatic joints

title: L15.3 — Joint-Space and Cartesian Motion Quiz

questions.questionText: How is motion executed when commanding a robot in "Joint-Space"?

options.text: The tool tip is forced to draw a perfect straight line in 3D space
Each joint angle is commanded to move directly from its start angle to its target angle
The controller continuously computes matrix inversions during the motion
The end-effector remains stationary while the base rotates

questions.questionText: What is a key characteristic of Cartesian-Space motion planning?

options.text: The end-effector follows a defined trajectory path (e.g., a straight line) in x, y, z space
It eliminates the need for inverse kinematics calculations
Individual joint velocities remain completely constant throughout the movement
It can only be performed on 2-DOF robotic arms

questions.questionText: Why is Cartesian-Space motion commonly preferred during the final approach of an object insertion task?

options.text: It uses significantly less motor power than joint-space motion
It allows the tool to move in a straight line, avoiding unexpected lateral collisions
It prevents the joint motors from generating torque
It guarantees that joint limits will never be exceeded

questions.questionText: What is a trajectory in robotic motion control?

options.text: A single static point in Cartesian space
A planned sequence of positions over time, constrained by velocity and acceleration limits
The total mechanical weight of the robotic links
The electrical schematic connecting joint controllers

questions.questionText: What is a major disadvantage of purely Joint-Space motion when moving near obstacles?

options.text: The tool path in physical space curves and can be difficult to predict visually
It requires heavy matrix operations on every control loop
It prevents the arm from reaching its joint limits
Motors cannot decelerate smoothly at the end of the motion

questions.questionText: Which gripper type utilizes two opposing fingers moving in parallel synchronization to clamp flat or box-like objects?

options.text: Vacuum gripper
Parallel-jaw gripper
Magnetic gripper
Soft compliant gripper

questions.questionText: In what manufacturing scenario is a vacuum/suction gripper typically preferred over a mechanical jaw gripper?

options.text: Handling heavy, smooth, non-porous flat sheet metal or glass panels
Picking up oily, porous wooden logs
Precision assembly of micro-screws
Grasping cylindrical rods along their length

questions.questionText: What advantage do soft/compliant grippers offer over rigid metal grippers?

options.text: They exert maximum possible crushing force
They can passively conform to delicate or irregularly shaped items without damaging them
They require zero electrical power or pneumatic input
They completely eliminate friction during manipulation

questions.questionText: Which type of gripper mechanism is restricted strictly to handling ferrous materials?

options.text: Multi-finger articulated hand
Pneumatic vacuum pad
Magnetic gripper
Parallel-jaw gripper

questions.questionText: Which factor is LEAST critical when selecting an appropriate gripper for a specific application?

options.text: Object mass and surface texture
Object fragility and shape
Color of the workspace mounting frame
Required grip force and actuation speed

title: L15.5 — Grasping and Contact Forces Quiz

questions.questionText: What fundamental equation represents the force due to gravity acting downward on an object of mass 'm'?

options.text: F = m / g
W = m * g
W = m * a^2

questions.questionText: In friction-based grasping, what role does friction play at the contact points?

options.text: It causes the object to rotate out of the grip
It counteracts downward gravitational force to prevent slippage
It decreases the required normal force to zero
It pushes the gripper jaws apart

questions.questionText: What distinguishes a "stable grasp" from an "unstable grasp"?

options.text: A stable grasp uses maximum possible force at all times
A stable grasp prevents unwanted translation, rotation, or slippage under disturbance forces
An unstable grasp requires no contact forces from the fingers
A stable grasp only works on perfectly spherical objects

questions.questionText: Why is applying maximum possible grip force generally considered bad practice in robotic manipulation?

options.text: It degrades motor efficiency and can crush fragile objects
It reduces friction between the fingers and the object
It shifts the center of mass outside the robot workspace
It forces the robot controller into joint-space mode

questions.questionText: What parameter determines the coefficient of static friction between a gripper finger and an object?

options.text: The speed of the joint actuators
The surface materials and textures of both contacting bodies
The length of the primary robot arm link
The inverse kinematics algorithm chosen

title: L15.6 — Static Equilibrium of the Arm Quiz

questions.questionText: What two vector summation conditions must be satisfied for a system to be in static equilibrium?

options.text: Sum of velocities = 0 and sum of accelerations = 0
Sum of forces = 0 and sum of torques = 0
Sum of joint angles = 180 degrees and sum of link lengths = 1 meter
Sum of potential energy = 0 and sum of kinetic energy = 1

questions.questionText: How is torque (moment) calculated mathematically when a force is applied perpendicular to a lever arm?

options.text: Torque = Force / Distance
Torque = Force * Distance
Torque = Mass * Velocity
Torque = Force + Distance

questions.questionText: How does fully extending a robot arm horizontally affect the torque required at the shoulder joint to hold a constant payload?

options.text: Shoulder joint torque decreases to zero
Shoulder joint torque increases because the lever arm distance increases
Shoulder joint torque remains completely unchanged
Shoulder joint torque becomes negative

questions.questionText: Why must the weight of the robot's own mechanical links be included in static torque analysis?

options.text: Link masses contribute to gravitational torque acting on upstream joint motors
Link masses convert revolute joints into prismatic joints
Link masses eliminate friction at the end-effector
Link masses cancel out external payload forces

questions.questionText: Where does the gravitational force of a uniform link act in a static free-body diagram?

options.text: At the tip of the end-effector
At the center of mass of the link
At the base coordinate frame
Exclusively at the motor output shaft

title: L15.7 — Position Control and Force Control Quiz

questions.questionText: What is the main objective of a position control system in robotics?

options.text: To regulate the exact force exerted during mechanical contact
To drive joints or the end-effector toward target spatial coordinates while minimizing position error
To increase motor temperature
To measure external electrical resistance

questions.questionText: In what situation is pure position control problematic or unsafe?

options.text: Moving through free, unobstructed air
Making contact with a rigid, unyielding surface of uncertain location
Calibrating encoder home positions
Executing forward kinematics calculations

questions.questionText: What is the primary function of force control during grasping?

options.text: To accelerate the arm to top speed
To measure and regulate contact forces to avoid dropping or damaging objects
To continuously invert the Jacobian matrix
To override joint limit switches

questions.questionText: Which control strategy uses feedback from force/torque sensors to yield softly when meeting mechanical resistance?

options.text: Open-loop step control
Compliant or impedance force control
Pure kinematic position control
Fixed joint angle control

questions.questionText: In a standard pick-and-place operation, what is the recommended control transition sequence?

options.text: Force control during transit in air, then position control during clamping
Position control to reach and approach, transitioning to force control upon object contact
Force control exclusively from start to finish
Open-loop control throughout the entire trajectory

questions.questionText: What is the primary purpose of defining a "pre-grasp" pose during the approach phase?

options.text: To calibrate the color vision camera
To position the open gripper safely near the object before final linear alignment
To turn off the robot joint motors
To measure ambient room temperature

questions.questionText: Which phase immediately follows "Align" in a standard pick-and-place state sequence?

options.text: Place
Transfer
Grasp
Return

questions.questionText: Why is vertical "Lift" performed before horizontal "Transfer" of a grasped workpiece?

options.text: To verify the object is clear of the supporting surface and avoid scraping obstacles
To reset joint encoders to zero
To switch from Cartesian space to joint space permanently
To allow suction cups to fill with ambient air

questions.questionText: What should every state in a robust pick-and-place state machine explicitly contain?

options.text: An infinite retry loop
An action, a completion condition, and a failure/timeout condition
A direct call to forward kinematics only
A hardcoded delay of at least 60 seconds

questions.questionText: What is the final operational step in a complete pick-and-place sequence?

options.text: Aligning over target
Closing gripper jaws
Lowering, releasing the object, and confirming release
Lifting payload clear of table

questions.questionText: In a basic 2D two-link planar arm simulation model, how is each link represented geometrically?

options.text: By a 3D mesh file with textures
By a rigid line segment of specified scalar length L
By a point mass at the origin
By a differential equation of fluid flow

questions.questionText: In a Python simulation, what trigonometric formulas compute the end-effector coordinate (x, y) for a 2-link arm with joint angles θ1 and θ2?

options.text: x = L1*cos(θ1) + L2*cos(θ1+θ2), y = L1*sin(θ1) + L2*sin(θ1+θ2)
x = L1*tan(θ1), y = L2*tan(θ2)
x = L1+L2, y = θ1+θ2
x = L1*sin(θ1), y = L2*cos(θ2)

questions.questionText: Which popular Python plotting library is commonly used for rendering 2D kinematic arm visualizations and animations?

options.text: NumPy
Matplotlib
Pandas
SciPy

questions.questionText: In a simulation workflow, how is "grasping" typically modeled when hardware contact physics are omitted?

options.text: By setting link lengths to zero
By setting object coordinates equal to the end-effector coordinate upon grip trigger
By clearing all plot axes and ending the program
By doubling the frame rate of the animation

questions.questionText: Why is software simulation recommended before running new control code on physical robot arms?

options.text: Simulation guarantees physical motors will never wear out
Simulation permits safe debugging of kinematics, trajectories, and logic without risk of equipment damage
Simulation eliminates the need for sensor feedback in real hardware
Python code cannot run on real hardware controllers

questions.questionText: What software design pattern is widely used to organize pick-and-place execution logic into distinct operational modes?

options.text: Finite State Machine (FSM)
Singleton Pattern
Model-View-Controller (MVC)
Factory Pattern

questions.questionText: In state machine logic, what triggers the state transition from "GRASP" to "LIFT"?

options.text: Timer reaching 24 hours
Confirmation of a successful grip (e.g., force threshold reached or jaws closed)
Joint 1 reaching maximum speed
Program crash error flag

questions.questionText: Consider the logic: `if state == "APPROACH" and at_pregrasp_pose: state = "GRASP"`. What is `at_pregrasp_pose`?

options.text: A constant string variable
A boolean condition checking if position error to pre-grasp pose is within acceptable tolerance
The maximum torque limit of the wrist motor
A physical sensor mounted on the gripper tip

questions.questionText: What is a major software engineering benefit of using a state machine over a long procedural script for robot control?

options.text: It increases program execution speed by 100x
It makes control flow modular, easy to debug, and simple to handle timeouts or errors
It automatically converts Python code into hardware wiring diagrams
It bypasses all inverse kinematics requirements

questions.questionText: Why are safety timeouts critical inside pick-and-place program state loops?

options.text: To make the robot move faster during production
To prevent the robot from hanging indefinitely in a state if a target pose or sensor condition fails
To automatically shut off power every 5 minutes
To force the robot into Cartesian space mode
